result.journal: Inf. Secur. J. A Glob. Perspect.
result.keywords: This article examines how local and global machine learning models can be combined to analyze habituation in security warning systems deployed in rapidly growing urban environments. Using a weighted fusion of localized and generalized support vector machine classifiers, the study models user response patterns to repeated alerts across different neighborhood contexts and compares local-only, global-only, and integrated approaches. The proposed framework is validated with cross-validation and applied to simulate changes in warning effectiveness over time in a metropolitan case study in Iran. Results indicate that blending local and global probabilistic outputs improves prediction accuracy and supports more adaptive urban cybersecurity interventions.
result.title: Integrating Local and Global Models for Habituation in Urban Security Warnings.
